props.title: Infernal Affairs
props.initialSlug: Hong Kong crime thriller that inspired The Departed

sections.content: Infernal Affairs revolutionized Hong Kong crime cinema with its intricate cat-and-mouse game between an undercover cop and a gangster's mole. Directors Andrew Lau and Alan Mak crafted a masterclass in sustained tension that influenced crime thrillers globally, most notably Martin Scorsese's The Departed (2006). The film's exploration of dual identities and moral corruption in Hong Kong's police force created a template that countless Asian crime thrillers would follow, including its own sequels and Cold War (2012). Tony Leung and Andy Lau deliver career-defining performances as men trapped in false identities, their psychological deterioration reflecting Hong Kong's pre-handover anxiety.

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond Asian cinema. Its taut plotting and themes of identity crisis inspired a wave of sophisticated police thrillers like New World (2013) and The Chaser (2008). The claustrophobic rooftop sequences and surveillance tension became blueprint moments for modern crime cinema, echoed in films like Eye in the Sky (2007) and Cold Eyes (2013). The psychological toll of undercover work, so masterfully portrayed in Infernal Affairs, became a central theme in later works like Confession of Pain (2006). SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Crime Cinema

Infernal Affairs' technical innovations transformed action filmmaking in Asia. The film's use of tight close-ups during dialogue scenes, rapid cross-cutting between parallel storylines, and moody urban cinematography influenced works like Beast Stalker (2008) and Breaking News (2004). Its exploration of police corruption and institutional rot resonated deeply in Hong Kong cinema, leading to spiritual successors like PTU (2003) and Line Walker (2016).
